event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: KLAC’s 2021-08-06 Form 10-K provides extensive, recent-event (≤18 months) disclosures that link the COVID-19 pandemic to material operational, financial and strategic threats.  The filing identifies concrete, enterprise-wide exposures: (i) supply-chain shortages, longer component lead-times and cost inflation; (ii) labour and logistics constraints caused by travel bans, quarantines and remote-work inefficiencies; (iii) the possibility of plant shutdowns under government mandates; (iv) weakened customer liquidity, order push-outs and demand volatility; and (v) constraints already felt in FY-2021 ("new constraints in our supply chain").  These statements are largely forward-looking but also acknowledge current impacts, therefore combining existing and potential risk.  Mitigations—vaccines, safety protocols, continued site operations—are mentioned but characterised as uncertain or insufficient to offset risk.  Given the Time-Decay Principle (event <3 yrs old), the potential for ‘materially adverse’ harm, the presence of specific operational mechanisms (supply chain, labour, demand) and only partial mitigations, individual evidence snippets generally merit high (7-10) scores, moderated where language is conditional or mitigation is explicit.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 Pandemic Risks • shortages or disruption in the supply chain could affect our ability to timely process components for our products; • travel bans or quarantine requirements could delay our ability to install or service our products; • governmental orders or employee exposure could cause manufacturing stoppages for us or our customers or suppliers; • reduced demand for our products, delivery pushouts or cancellations of orders by our customers; • increased costs or inability to acquire components necessary for the manufacture of our products; • absence of liquidity at customers and suppliers; and • loss of efficiencies due to remote working requirements for our employees.

components.reason: Enumerates multiple critical operational risks (supply-chain, logistics, manufacturing stoppage).
Highlights direct financial demand risks (reduced demand, cancellations).
Includes liquidity concerns for customers and suppliers, expanding systemic exposure.
States potential cost inflation and remote-work inefficiency.
Uses conditional wording ('could'), slightly reducing immediacy.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive list of severe, pandemic-driven threats across operations, finance and workforce justifies a high score; conditional language tempers it slightly.

evidence_list.snippet: The current COVID-19 pandemic and the potential aftereffects from it could materially harm our business, financial condition and results of operations.

components.reason: Explicit statement that pandemic can 'materially harm' business and financials.
Links to broad corporate impact (operations, financial condition, results).
Recency of event (within 3 years).
Uses 'could', signalling forward-looking uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct assertion of material harm elevates severity, though conditional language prevents maximum score.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused substantial global disruptions, including in the jurisdictions where we conduct business and may cause additional disruptions in the future, which are impossible to predict.

components.reason: Acknowledges actual, ongoing disruptions already experienced.
Highlights unpredictability and potential for future impact.
Covers global scope across KLAC jurisdictions.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Combines confirmed historical impact with forward uncertainty across all geographies—high severity.

evidence_list.snippet: While all of our global sites are currently operational, any local pandemic outbreaks could require us to temporarily curtail production levels or temporarily cease operations based on government mandates.

components.reason: Identifies risk of production curtailment/cessation due to outbreaks.
Ties risk to external government mandates—uncontrollable factor.
States current full operations, signalling partial mitigation.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential shutdown risk is serious, but current full operations and conditional wording lower immediate severity.

evidence_list.snippet: However, given our global operations, we are unable to predict how widely utilized the vaccines ultimately will be and whether they will be effective in preventing the spread of COVID-19 (including its variant strains).

components.reason: Emphasises uncertainty over vaccine uptake and efficacy, sustaining risk horizon.
Mentions variant strains, extending potential impact duration.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows persistent uncertainty despite mitigation attempts; moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, although economic activity has begun to improve in recent months from the global reduction in economic activity in calendar year 2020 caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, the pace of economic recovery remains uneven in various geographies, and the resumption of growth has caused us to experience new constraints in our supply chain as discussed below.

components.reason: Admits continued uneven recovery across geographies.
Notes new supply-chain constraints already being experienced.
Acknowledges some economic improvement (mitigation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Demonstrates real supply-chain impact and uneven recovery; partial mitigation keeps score mid-range.

evidence_list.snippet: Some of the risks associated with the pandemic or a worsening of the pandemic in the future include: • cancellation or reduction of routes available from common carriers, which may cause delays in our ability to deliver or service our products or receive components from suppliers necessary to manufacture or service our products; • shortages or disruption in the supply chain could affect our ability to procure components for our products on a timely basis or at all, or could require us to commit to increased purchases and provide longer lead times to secure critical components, which could increase inventory obsolescence risk; • travel bans or the requirement to quarantine for a lengthy period after entering a jurisdiction, which may delay our ability to install the products we sell or service those products following installation; • governmental orders or employee exposure requiring us, our customers or our suppliers to discontinue manufacturing products at our respective facilities for a period of time; • reduced demand for our products, delivery pushouts or cancellation of orders by our customers caused by a global recession resulting from the pandemic and the measures implemented by authorities to slow the spread of COVID-19; • increased costs or inability to acquire components necessary for the manufacture of our products due to reduced availability; • absence of liquidity at customers and suppliers caused by disruptions from the pandemic, which may hamper the ability of customers to pay for the products they purchase on time or at all, or hamper the ability of our suppliers to continue to supply components to us in a timely manner or at all; and • loss of efficiencies due to remote working requirements for our employees.

components.reason: Details multiple operational threats (logistics, supply, manufacturing stoppage).
Includes demand-side recession risk and customer cancellations.
Lists cost inflation and inventory obsolescence.
Mentions liquidity crunch for customers/suppliers.
Forward-looking with ‘could’ language.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad inventory of severe risks across operations, demand and finance warrants high score despite conditional wording.

evidence_list.snippet: If any of the foregoing risks occur or intensify during this pandemic, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially adversely affected.

components.reason: Explicitly warns of ‘materially adversely’ affected outcomes.
Ties directly to business, financial condition and results.
Conditional phrasing ‘if…occur’ reduces certainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong materiality language but fully contingent, leading to mid-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: natural disasters, health epidemics, acts of terrorism or war or other catastrophic events could significantly disrupt our operations for lengthy periods of time;

components.reason: Identifies epidemics as a disruption source with prolonged impact.
Grouped with other catastrophes—generic mention.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic epidemic reference with no pandemic-specific detail yields low score.

evidence_list.snippet: Disruption of our manufacturing facilities or other operations, or in the operations of our customers, due to earthquake, flood, other natural catastrophic events, health epidemics or terrorism could result in cancellation of orders, delays in deliveries or other business activities, or loss of customers and could seriously harm our business.

components.reason: Epidemics listed as cause of serious harm including lost customers.
Generic multi-hazard clause dilutes specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: States serious consequences but only generic to epidemics; moderate-low severity.

evidence_list.snippet: Impact of COVID-19 Events surrounding the COVID-19 pandemic had resulted in a reduction in economic activity across the globe in calendar year 2020.

components.reason: Confirms realised global economic reduction affecting KLAC’s market.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Signals actual macro-economic harm already experienced; moderately high relevance.

evidence_list.snippet: The resumption of growth has caused us to experience new constraints in our supply chain.

components.reason: Indicates current supply-chain constraints attributable to pandemic recovery phase.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Demonstrates ongoing operational impact despite recovery; moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: Supply lead times are extended and shortages have sometimes required us to increase our purchase commitments to secure critical components on a timely basis.

components.reason: Describes concrete, current supply shortages and extended lead times.
Forced to increase commitments, implying financial exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides specific evidence of cost and supply risk presently materialising; above-average severity.
